PROJECT NO. 58481
(STAFF Discussion Draft) 
Draft NEW 16 TAC §25.194
Staff of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (commission staff) requests comments on the attached discussion draft, which would propose new 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) §25.194 relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards.  Draft §25.194 would set forth the standards and criteria for an electric utility, including a municipally owned utility and electric cooperative, to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network. 

Public Comments
Interested persons may file comments on this discussion draft electronically through the interchange on the commission’s website or by submitting a paper copy to Central Records, Public Utility Commission of Texas, 1701 North Congress Avenue, P.O. Box 13326, Austin, Texas 78711-3326.  Comments must be filed by December 19, 2025.  Comments should be organized in a manner consistent with the organization of the discussion draft.  All comments should refer to Project Number 58481.

In addition to general comments on the text of the discussion draft, commission staff invites interested persons to address the following specific questions: 
Should the commission define parameters for determining whether a large load customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request?  If so, how should the commission define those parameters?
Proposed subsections (c)(3), (e)(3), and (h)(3) require the disclosure of specific information related to a substantially similar request for interconnection and allows a large load customer to anonymize competitively sensitive details.  Should the commission list what is and is not competitively sensitive (e.g., load zone is not competitively sensitive information)?  If so, what information should and should not be considered competitively sensitive such that the interconnecting utility and ERCOT can identify whether there is a duplicate request, or a request is unlikely to materialize? 
Should the commission require a large load customer to notify the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT of any change to information that is initially disclosed in response to this rule or only material changes to the information disclosed?  If only material changes, how should “material change” be defined?
Proposed subsection (k)(1) authorizes an interconnecting electric utility to refund 20% of a large load customer’s security after energization and ratably as the large load customer meets the milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization of its contracted load.  Should the commission standardize the rate for refund for reaching milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization (e.g., 20% for each year of operations until the full amount of security is refunded)?  If so, how should the commission standardize the refund?
Are changes to the commission’s other substantive rules necessary to align with this rulemaking?  If so, what changes need to be made to which rules?

Each set of comments should include a standalone executive summary as the last page of the filing.  This executive summary must be clearly labeled with the submitting entity’s name and should include a bulleted list covering each substantive recommendation made in the comments. 

Questions concerning this notice should be referred to Jessie Horn, Rules and Projects Division at jessie.horn@puc.texas.gov.  

§25.194.  Large Load Interconnection Standards.
(a)	Purpose and Scope.  This section sets forth the standards and criteria for an electric utility, including a municipally owned utility and electric cooperative, to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network.

(b)	Definitions.  The following words and terms, when used in this section, have the following meanings unless the context indicates otherwise:
(1)	Backup generating facilities -- Generation facilities that are not capable of exporting energy to the ERCOT transmission system and that, in aggregate, can serve at least 50% of on-site contracted peak demand.
(2)	Contracted peak demand – the total peak demand that a large load customer requests that an interconnecting electric utility serve at a site as stated in an executed and securitized discretionary services agreement or intermediate agreement.
(3)	Discretionary services agreement -- An agreement, executed and securitized by a large load customer and interconnecting electric utility after the interconnecting electric utility completes the large load interconnection study and before the interconnecting electric utility submits the study to ERCOT, that, at a minimum, satisfies subsection (d) of this section.
(4)	End-use customer -- the legal entity that eventually will consume the electricity for its operations at the site subject to an interconnection request.
(5)	Interconnecting electric utility -- The electric utility, municipally owned utility, or electric cooperative that owns and operates the facilities necessary to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network.  
(6)	Intermediate agreement -- An agreement, executed and securitized by a large load customer and interconnecting electric utility after the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT complete the necessary transmission studies, that, at a minimum, satisfies subsection (h) of this section.
(7)	Large load customer -- A customer requesting a new or expanded interconnection where the customer’s total peak demand at a single site is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts (MW).  
(9)	Large load interconnection study -- a set of studies required in the ERCOT protocols to determine compliance with ERCOT planning requirements and the scope of upgrades to existing facilities or new facilities needed to serve a large load customer requesting interconnection.
(10)	Project developer -- An entity that develops a real estate site and that is not the end-use customer as defined in this section.  
(11)	Requested peak demand -- the total peak demand that a large load customer requests, prior to executing and securitizing a discretionary services agreement, intermediate agreement, or interconnection agreement, that an interconnecting electric utility serve.

(c)	Disclosures and study fee upon receipt of interconnection request.  Prior to conducting a large load interconnection study, the interconnecting electric utility must obtain the disclosures and study fee under this subsection from a large load customer seeking to interconnect in the electric utility’s retail delivery service area.
(1)	Project developer or end-use customer.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting utility whether the customer is a project developer or an end-use customer.
(2)	Site control.  A large load customer must demonstrate site control for the proposed load location through provision of one of the following property interests to the interconnecting electric utility:
(A)	a legally binding option to purchase or lease for the proposed load location; 
(B)	a signed and executed lease agreement for the proposed load location; or 
(C)	a deed for the proposed load location.
(3)	Substantially similar interconnection request.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service, the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the interconnection request.
(A)	 A large load customer that is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service, the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the interconnection request must disclose the following information to the interconnecting electric utility:
(i)	the location, including the load zone, of the substantially similar interconnection request;
(ii)	the size of the substantially similar interconnection request;
(iii)	the anticipated timing of energization of the substantially similar interconnection request; and
(iv)	the interconnecting electric utility for the substantially similar interconnection request.
(B)	A large load customer that discloses a substantially similar interconnection request under this subsection may anonymize competitively sensitive details in its disclosure to the interconnecting electric utility.
(C)	An interconnecting electric utility must not sell, share, or disclose information submitted to the utility under this subsection other than a disclosure to the commission or ERCOT.
(4)	Schedule for phased energization of requested peak demand.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility the expected schedule, including the month and year, for phased energization of the requested peak demand expressed in MW and megavolt-ampere reactive (MVAr) units. 
(5)	Backup generating facilities.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer plans to have on-site backup generating facilities.  If the large load customer plans to have on-site backup generating facilities, the large load customer must also disclose the following information:
(A)	the number of backup generating facilities;
(B)	the nameplate capacity of each of the backup generating facilities;
(C)	the fuel source and operational characteristics of each of the backup generating facilities; and
(D)	how quickly each of the large load customer’s backup generating facilities can turn on to begin serving the load.
(6)	Dynamic modeling.  A large load customer must provide a dynamic load model to the interconnecting electric utility.
(7)	Study fee.  A large load customer must pay a study fee for the interconnecting electric utility’s and ERCOT’s costs to conduct the large load interconnection study.
(A)	A large load customer with requested peak demand that is equal to 75MW and less than 250MW must pay a study fee not less than $114,000 to the interconnecting electric utility for transmission studies performed by the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT.  If the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s combined costs to conduct the large load interconnection study fee is expected to exceed $114,000, the large load customer must pay a study fee in the amount of the interconnecting electric utility’s and ERCOT’s expected costs to conduct the large load interconnection study.  
(B)	A large load customer with requested peak demand that is equal to or greater than 250 MW must pay a study fee not less than $314,000.  If the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s combined costs to conduct the large load interconnection study fee is expected to exceed $314,000, the large load customer must pay a study fee in the amount of the interconnecting electric utility’s and ERCOT’s expected costs to conduct the large load interconnection study.  
(C)	Beginning in 2027, the commission will adjust the values under this subsection on January 1 of each calendar year.
(i)	The annual adjustment will be proportional to the third quarter percentage change in the national Consumer Price Index (CPI) published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.
(ii)	The executive director must designate a substitute index to be used as a reference for adjustments if the CPI becomes unavailable.
(iii)	If the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s combined costs to conduct the large load interconnection study fee is expected to exceed the value of the annual adjustment, the large load customer must pay a study fee in the amount of the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s expected costs to conduct the large load interconnection study.
(D)	The interconnecting electric utility must remit payment to ERCOT, on behalf of the large load customer, for ERCOT’s large load interconnection study fee.

(d)	Large load interconnection study.  Not later than 30 days after receipt of the required disclosures, financial commitment, and study fee required under subsection (c) of this section, the interconnecting electric utility must coordinate with ERCOT to conduct a large load interconnection study.    
(1)	Within 5 days of a change to the information disclosed under subsection (c) of this section, the large load customer must notify the interconnecting electric utility of the change.  
(2)	A large load customer that requests additional capacity to serve an increase to the requested or contracted peak demand after the interconnecting electric utility initiates the large load interconnection study must pay an additional study fee based on the interconnecting electric utility’s and ERCOT’s costs to complete the large load interconnection study for the total requested or contracted peak demand.  The large load customer must pay the additional study fee or withdraw its request for interconnection within 10 days of being notified of the additional study fee.  Failure to pay the additional study fee may be treated as a withdrawal of the request for additional capacity at the site of the interconnection request.
(3)	The interconnecting electric utility must notify the large load customer when the utility completes the large load interconnection study.

(e)	Discretionary services agreement.  Before the interconnecting electric utility submits the large load interconnection study to ERCOT, the large load customer must execute and securitize a discretionary services agreement that, at a minimum, includes the updated disclosures and financial commitments under this subsection.  
(1)	Project developer or end-use customer.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting utility whether the customer is a project developer or an end-use customer.
(2)	Site control.  A large load customer must demonstrate site control for the proposed load location through provision of one of the following property interests to the interconnecting electric utility:
(A)	a legally and financially binding option to purchase or lease for the proposed load location for the duration of at least 50% of the expected time to reach the peak demand;
(B)	a signed and executed lease agreement for the proposed load location for the duration of at least 50% of the expected time to reach the peak demand; or 
(C)	a deed for the proposed load location.
(3)	Substantially similar interconnection request.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service, the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the interconnection request.
(A)	 A large load customer that is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the interconnection request must disclose the following information to the interconnecting electric utility:
(i)	the location, including the load zone, of the substantially similar interconnection request;
(ii)	the size of the substantially similar interconnection request;
(iii)	the anticipated timing of energization of the substantially similar interconnection request; and
(iv)	the interconnecting electric utility for the substantially similar interconnection request.
(B)	A large load customer that discloses a substantially similar interconnection request under this subsection may anonymize competitively sensitive details in its disclosure to the interconnecting electric utility.
(C)	An interconnecting electric utility must not sell, share, or disclose information submitted to the utility under this subsection other than a disclosure to the commission or ERCOT.
(4)	Site-related studies and engineering services.  A large load customer must submit to the interconnecting electric utility the large load customer’s plans, expected timing, and progress for site-related studies and engineering services required for project development before energization (e.g., water, wastewater, or gas).  The submission must be accompanied by an attestation by an officer or official with binding authority over the large load customer stating that the information contained in the submission is complete and accurate at the time the attestation is signed.  A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the interconnecting electric utility when requested.
(5)	State and local regulatory approvals.  A large load customer must submit to the interconnecting electric utility describing the large load customer’s plans, expected timing, and current progress for obtaining state and local regulatory approvals required for development before energization (e.g., water, air, or backup generation permits, or city or county building permits).  The submission must be accompanied by an attestation by an officer or official with binding authority over the large load customer attesting that the information contained in the submission is complete and accurate at the time the attestation is signed.  A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the interconnecting electric utility when requested.
(6)	Schedule for phased energization of contracted peak demand.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility the expected schedule, including the month and year, for phased energization of the contracted peak demand expressed in MW and MVAr units. 
(7)	Backup generating facilities.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer plans to have on-site backup generating facilities.  If the large load customer plans to have on-site backup generating facilities, the large load customer must also disclose the following information:
(A)	the number of backup generating facilities;
(B)	the nameplate capacity of each of the backup generating facilities;
(C)	the fuel source and operational characteristics of each of the backup generating facilities; and
(D)	how quickly each of the backup generating facilities can turn on to begin serving the load.
(8)	Financial security on a dollar per MW basis.  A large load customer must pay financial security to the interconnecting electric utility $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand.  
(A)	Beginning in 2027, the commission will adjust the $50,000 value on January 1 of each calendar year.
(i)	The annual adjustment will be proportional to the third quarter percentage change in the national Consumer Price Index (CPI)published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.
(ii)	The executive director must designate a substitute index to be used as a reference for adjustments if the CPI becomes unavailable.
(B)	The interconnecting electric utility may accept the following forms of payment for the financial security:
(i)	cash collateral;
(ii)	corporate or parental guaranty, only if the corporation or parent corporation has a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm; or 
(iii)	a letter of credit issued by a bank with a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm.

(f)	Submission of large load interconnection study to ERCOT.  Not later than 7 days after the large load customer executes and securitizes a discretionary services agreement, the interconnecting electric utility must submit the large load interconnection study to ERCOT.  The interconnecting electric utility must cancel the interconnection requested and notify ERCOT of the cancellation if the large load customer fails to execute and securitize a discretionary services agreement within 30 days of the interconnecting electric utility’s completion of the large load interconnection study. 

(g)	Notification of additional study.  Not later than 30 days after receipt of the large load interconnection study from the interconnecting electric utility, ERCOT must notify the interconnecting electric utility whether a large load customer’s interconnection requires additional study.  
(1)	ERCOT’s notification to the interconnecting electric utility must include the following information:
(A)	the reason additional study is necessary;
(B)	what additional study is required; and
(C)	an estimated timeline for completing the additional study.
(2)	Upon receipt of ERCOT’s notification that additional study is necessary, the interconnecting electric utility must provide a copy of ERCOT’s notification to the large load customer. 
(3)	The interconnecting electric utility must provide a large load customer timely information related to communications that the interconnecting electric utility receives from ERCOT about the large load customer’s interconnection request.
(4)	The interconnecting electric utility must inform the large load customer of the costs for the additional study.  Within 10 days of being notified that additional study is necessary, the large load customer must either pay the costs for the additional study or withdraw its request for interconnection.  Failure to pay the costs for the additional study within 10 days may be treated as a withdrawal of the interconnection request.

(h)	Intermediate agreement.  Not later than 180 days after the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT complete the large load interconnection study for a large load customer, the large load customer must execute and securitize an intermediate agreement with the interconnecting electric utility that, at a minimum, includes the updated disclosures and financial commitments under this subsection.  The interconnecting electric utility must cancel the interconnection request and notify ERCOT of the cancellation if the large load customer fails to execute and securitize an intermediate agreement under this subsection within 180 days of the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s completion of all necessary transmission studies to interconnect the large load customer.  
(1)	Project developer or end-use customer.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting utility whether the customer is a project developer or an end-use customer.  If the large load customer is a project developer, the large load customer must disclose whether an end-use customer has signed a contract to take service at the location where the project developer is requesting interconnection.
(2)	Site control.  A large load customer must demonstrate site control for the load location through provision of one of the following property interests to the interconnecting electric utility:
(A)	a signed and executed lease agreement for the load location that is valid through the year that the large load customer’s contracted peak demand is expected to be reached; or
(B)	a deed for the load location.
(3)	Substantially similar request.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service, the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the interconnection request.
(A)	A large load customer that is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service, the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the interconnection request must disclose the following information to the interconnecting electric utility:
(i)	the location of the substantially similar interconnection request;
(ii)	the size of the substantially similar interconnection request;
(iii)	the anticipated timing of energization of the substantially similar interconnection request; and
(iv)	the interconnecting electric utility for the substantially similar interconnection request.
(B)	A large load customer that discloses a substantially similar interconnection request under this subsection may anonymize the competitively sensitive details in its disclosure to the interconnecting electric utility.
(C)	An interconnecting electric utility must not sell, share, or disclose information submitted to the utility under this subsection other than a disclosure to the commission or ERCOT.
(4)	Site-related studies and engineering services.  A large load customer must submit to the interconnecting electric utility the large load customer’s plans, expected timing, and progress for site-related studies and engineering services required for project development before energization (e.g., water, wastewater, or gas).  The submission must be accompanied by an attestation by an officer or official with binding authority over the large load customer attesting that the information contained in the submission is complete and accurate at the time the attestation is signed.  A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the interconnecting electric utility when requested.
(5)	State and local regulatory approvals.  A large load customer must submit to the interconnecting electric utility the large load customer’s plans, expected timing, and current progress for obtaining state and local regulatory approvals required for development before energization (e.g., water, air, or backup generation permits, or city or county building permits).  The submission must be accompanied by an attestation by an officer or official with binding authority over the large load customer attesting that the information contained in the submission is complete and accurate at the time the attestation is signed.  A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the interconnecting electric utility when requested.
(6)	Schedule for phased energization of contracted peak demand.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility the expected schedule, including the month and year, for phased energization of the contracted peak demand expressed in MW and MVAr units.
(7)	Backup generating facilities.  A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer plans to have on-site backup generating facilities.  If the large load customer plans to have on-site backup generating facilities, the large load customer must also disclose the following information:
(A)	the number of backup generating facilities;
(B)	the nameplate capacity of each of the backup generating facilities;
(C)	the fuel source and operational characteristics of each of the backup generating facilities; and
(D)	how quickly each of the backup generating facilities can turn on to begin serving the load.
(8)	Financial security for significant equipment or services.  Before the interconnecting electric utility procures equipment or services, a large load customer must pay financial security to the interconnecting utility in an amount equal to the interconnecting electric utility’s expected costs for equipment with a lead time of at least six months and services necessary to interconnect the large load customer.  The interconnecting electric utility may accept the following forms of payment for financial security for significant equipment or services:
(A)	cash collateral;
(B)	corporate or parental guaranty, only if the corporation or parent corporation has a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm; or 
(C)	a letter of credit issued by a bank with a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm.
(9)	Contribution in aid of construction (CIAC).  Before the interconnecting electric utility begins construction of facilities to interconnect a large load customer, a large load customer must pay CIAC in an amount that is equal to the interconnecting electric utility’s expected costs to interconnect the large load customer and that are directly attributable to interconnecting the large load customer.  
(A)	Costs directly attributable to interconnecting the large load customer include all costs associated with one or more new transmission lines built to interconnect the large load customer to the existing transmission network, including substation upgrades associated with interconnecting the new large load customer.  
(B)	Costs associated with system upgrades that would not be required but for the interconnecting large load customer are costs directly attributable to the interconnecting large load customer.  Where a system upgrade is necessary to serve multiple large load customers, such system upgrade costs must be pro-rated among those large load customers based on the contracted peak demand of each of those customers.  
(C)	For a large load customer that is interconnecting to an existing transmission asset, costs directly attributable to interconnecting the large load customer include a share of the original CIAC that another large load customer paid under this section.  The share of original CIAC must be calculated based on remaining net book value of the associated costs as a fraction of the original book value of those costs, and further pro-rated based on the share of contracted peak demand of the new large load customer as a fraction of the aggregate contracted peak demand of all large load customers associated with that transmission asset, including the new large load customer.  CIAC payments under this subsection must be credited to the previous large load customers that contributed to the previous CIAC payments, on an asset by asset basis, in proportion to those previous payments.
(D)	The interconnecting electric utility may accept the following forms of payment for CIAC:
(i)	cash collateral;
(ii)	corporate or parental guaranty, only if the corporation or parent corporation has a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm; or 
(iii)	a letter of credit issued by a bank with a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm.

(i)	Withdrawal of all or a portion of requested or contracted peak demand for interconnection.  A large load customer may withdraw all or a portion of its requested or contracted peak demand for interconnection by submitting its request in writing to the interconnecting electric utility.  
(1)	Not later than 10 days after receipt of a large load customer’s notice to withdraw all or a portion of requested or contracted peak demand for interconnection, the interconnecting electric utility must notify ERCOT via a method prescribed by ERCOT.  
(2)	Financial security that the large load customer paid must be applied to any outstanding amounts owed. 
(A)	Outstanding amounts owed include the following:
(i)	costs incurred by the interconnecting electric utility to fulfill the large load customer’s request for interconnection; 
(ii)	costs for equipment that the interconnecting electric utility procured and that cannot be canceled; 
(iii)	costs for construction that the interconnecting electric utility started and that cannot be canceled; and 
(iv)	costs for services that the interconnecting electric utilities initiated and that cannot be canceled.  
(B)	After applying financial security that the large load customer paid to any outstanding amounts owed, the interconnecting electric utility must refund the remaining balance to the large load customer.
(3)	CIAC that the large load customer paid is not refundable.

(j)	Reallocation of capacity.  An interconnecting electric utility must reallocate capacity of a large load customer that is energized and fails to satisfy, within 18 months, a milestone in its schedule for phased energization of the contracted peak demand.  An interconnecting electric utility that reallocates capacity under this subsection, must refund the balance of the large load customer’s security after drawing down for outstanding amounts owed and receiving financial security from another large load customer that the capacity is reallocated to serve.  Outstanding amounts owed include the following:
(1)	costs incurred by the interconnecting electric utility to fulfill the large load customer’s request for interconnection; 
(2)	costs for equipment that the interconnecting electric utility procured and that cannot be canceled; 
(3)	costs for construction that the interconnecting electric utility started and that cannot be canceled; and 
(4)	costs for services that the interconnecting electric utilities initiated and that cannot be canceled.  

(k)	Terms for refund of financial security for a large load customer that energizes.  An interconnecting electric utility must apply the financial security that a large load customer paid under this section to any amounts owed for costs incurred by the interconnecting electric utility to fulfill the large load customer’s request for interconnection.  
(1)	After applying the financial security to any amounts owed, the interconnecting electric utility must refund 20% of the remaining balance when the large load customer energizes and ratably as the large load customer meets the milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization of its contracted peak demand.  
(2)	The interconnecting electric utility must refund any remaining balance when the large load sustains operations for five years at the customer’s contracted peak demand.  

(l)	ERCOT operational standards.  
(1)	ERCOT may establish operational standards for large load customers to ensure system reliability.  
(2)	A large load customer must comply with operational standards, developed through ERCOT protocols, as a condition for interconnection and continued operation of the customer’s load.
